title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: Player Two (Anglo-Saxon) owns a CASTLE, 29 STONE_WALL segments, 2 gates and 4 GUARD_TOWERs: Harold's army at Senlac fought in the open on a ridge with no fortifications, and the stone donjon/castle is precisely the Norman innovation the Saxons lacked in 1066
Saxon STABLE (and the implied cavalry arm) is wrong: Harold's huscarls and fyrd fought dismounted; the Anglo-Saxon army used no mounted shock troops
GUARD_TOWER is a post-1066 fortification type in England, and stone gatehouses of this kind did not exist in Anglo-Saxon Sussex

4,800 TREE_OAK tiles create dense woodland over a battlefield that was open downland with marshy ground at the foot of the ridge - the map's own narration mentions a 'marshy field' the terrain does not deliver
Norman side is given a full TOWN_CENTER, MILL and HOUSEs; the Normans had a hastily thrown-up motte at Hastings, not a settled agricultural town, though the engine's building list partly excuses this
King Harold is represented by the generic KING unit, a non-combatant piece, rather than a fighting commander among his huscarls

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit skins and bonuses may render as Aztec, Japanese or Korean rather than Frankish/Teutonic (Norman) and Britons (Anglo-Saxon) — an entirely avoidable omission.

Player 2 owns a CASTLE, 29 STONE_WALL segments, 2 gates and 4 GUARD_TOWERs, plus 'Close Gates' and 'Gate Defense' triggers. Harold's army fought in the open on a bare ridge with no fortification whatsoever; the secondary objective 'Raze the Saxon Castle behind the ridge' invents a structure that did not exist.

4,800 TREE_OAK tiles and 25 cliffs on a 120x120 map turn Senlac into dense forest and broken cliff country; the field was open downland with marshy ground at the foot of the slope, which the narration itself mentions but the terrain contradicts.
The Saxon side is given a STABLE and an ARCHERY_RANGE despite the whole tactical point being that Harold's force was dismounted infantry with very few archers.

The feigned retreat — the scenario's stated central mechanic — exists only in dialogue text; the only Saxon movement triggers are a generic 'Enemy Patrol' and an 'Enemy Sortie' PATROL, with no lure-and-envelop scripting.

Norman force is 8 knights, 8 archers, 8 men-at-arms with a Town Center, houses and a Mill — a settlement economy rather than an invasion beachhead; no ships or camp palisade for the Pevensey/Hastings base referenced in the defeat text.

Timer victory at 900s awards the Normans the field merely for surviving to 'nightfall'; historically the battle was decided by Harold's death, and had the Saxons held until dark the invasion would have been in jeopardy.

Both players' civilizations are left as RANDOM, so architecture and unit bonuses may render the Normans as Aztecs or Koreans; Franks/Normans and Britons/Celts were available and should have been assigned explicitly.
4,800 oak trees on a 120x120 map turns the open downland of Senlac/Caldbec Hill into dense forest; the battle was fought on bare open slopes with marsh at the foot.

The Anglo-Saxon side is given a CASTLE, 29 STONE_WALL segments, 2 gates and 4 GUARD_TOWERs. Harold's army held an unfortified ridge; there was no fortification at Hastings, and the 'Raze the Saxon Castle' objective invents a structure outright.
Player 2 is given a STABLE and ARCHERY_RANGE, implying Saxon cavalry and archers when the sources are emphatic that Harold's army fought dismounted with almost no archery.
Norman archers (8) are underweighted relative to knights and infantry given that the missile arm was the decisive component of the combined assaults the brief itself stresses.
The defeat condition on the Norman TOWN_CENTER ('beachhead camp has fallen') invents a Saxon counter-raid on Hastings/Pevensey that never occurred during the battle.
The much-cited feigned retreat exists only in dialogue; no trigger (retreat/lure/re-attack scripting) models it, so the player never has to execute the tactic the brief names as the core mechanic.
The 900-second 'nightfall' victory lets the player win by merely surviving, whereas historically dusk came only after the shield wall had broken and Harold was dead.
